problem_and_intended_users_defined.rationale: P-055 addresses a narrow maintainer/contributor problem: explain the effective local CODEOWNERS file and conservative local hazards without pretending to replace GitHub's server-side parser, owner-access checks, branch protection or rulesets.

public_repository_or_distribution_surfac.rationale: The product is public as source, a reusable composite GitHub Action and the non-draft v0.10.0 release.

explicit_open_source_license.rationale: The public repository carries the MIT License covering the P-055 implementation.

complete_readme.rationale: Product documentation covers purpose, CLI/Action use, status semantics, GitHub authority boundary, architecture, privacy/security, accessibility/localization, recovery, release scope and limitations.

beginner_start_here_path.rationale: A dedicated beginner path explains what CODEOWNERS is, what the product checks, how to run it, how to interpret results, and when GitHub's own server-side checks remain necessary.

engineering_or_architecture_documentatio.rationale: The engineering path documents precedence, bounded parser scope, privacy-minimized evidence, threat model, hard-false claims, deterministic output and no-network/no-mutation architecture.

reproducible_installation_or_use_instruc.rationale: Consumers can run the dependency-light Python CLI or invoke the exact released @v0.10.0 composite Action; released-ref acceptance repeats the same-language execution and verifies deterministic evidence.

safety_scope_and_limitations.rationale: The product explicitly excludes authoritative GitHub syntax validation, owner/team existence or write-access verification, branch/ruleset enforcement, comprehensive ownership proof, repository-security certification and repository mutation.

recovery_or_rollback_guidance_for_mutati.rationale: P-055 is non-mutating; recovery is deletion of runner-temporary/external outputs and rerun. Any later maintainer CODEOWNERS changes are independent Git-reviewed edits with normal revert semantics.

tests_and_ci.rationale: Adversarial tests and hosted acceptance cover precedence, missing/invalid/valid states, symlink/path/size/output guards, privacy-minimized evidence, determinism, EN/ES guide truth consistency, exact-source release control and released-ref consumer immutability.

security_and_privacy_review.rationale: The review covers no token/API/network/subprocess/repository-code authority, no repository mutation, bounded file/path handling, owner-token non-retention, pattern hashing and privacy-safe public support.

accessibility_review.rationale: The interface is text-first JSON/Markdown with headings/lists and no color-only semantics. This is an applicability review, not a WCAG conformance or human assistive-technology claim.

multilingual_path_considered.rationale: English and Spanish beginner guides are executable product modes over the same language-neutral JSON evidence; released-ref acceptance verifies equal technical state, isolated output paths and distinct localized guides.

evidence_retained.rationale: Release-plan, publication and released-ref real-public evidence are retained with artifact IDs and GitHub-computed SHA-256 digests; the permanent completion record captures their meaning and non-claims.

version_tag_or_release_published.rationale: Public non-draft/non-prerelease v0.10.0 was published on 2026-08-16 and independently verified to resolve exactly to reviewed source 0615eaba32c9fe15a95230f61947694341cc4f89.

known_limitations_documented.rationale: Local conservative-parser scope, no authoritative GitHub syntax/access/enforcement validation, no complete ownership proof, no repository mutation/security guarantee and no WCAG/human multilingual acceptance claims are explicit.

contribution_and_issue_paths.rationale: General contribution guidance and a dedicated privacy-safe P-055 support/reproduction path exist on the public default branch.

canonical_handover_or_build_record_updat.rationale: The final completion record binds architecture, exact release source, governed publication, released-ref acceptance, retained evidence, security/privacy/accessibility review, limitations and recovery semantics.
